boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the three undrafted frozen records in the Maryland Campaign; MD003 Antietam keeps its existing draft unchanged. Preserve per-engagement dates: Harpers Ferry September 12–15, South Mountain September 14 and Shepherdstown September 19–20. The live NPS campaign heading does not replace any battle interval. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.rationale: Reported, computed and brigade-count estimates with different bases; none is adopted as a matched opening population. Crampton's Gap is a separate sub-action.

claims.value: Palfrey says McClellan had a copy of Lee's order at Frederick on the 13th. He reports that it has been said that the hour of receipt does not appear, and notes that McClellan's letter to Franklin giving the order's substance is dated 6.20 p.m. He says McLaws did not attach much importance to early indications of an advance, and that Lee's information seems to have come from Stuart.
claims.rationale: Retrospective reconstruction. The inspected source does not establish the receipt hour; Palfrey attributes the statement that it does not appear to others ('It has been said') and reports the Franklin letter's 6.20 p.m. date, which is not an inspected original and is not a receipt time. The Stuart attribution is Palfrey's hedged inference.

claims.value: Palfrey says McClellan ordered Franklin to move at daybreak rather than that night, and that no portion of the army was ordered to move that night, with the possible exception of Couch. He argues that had Franklin marched to the foot of the range that night he could have passed through it the next morning substantially unopposed, and that a night march of both wings would have given McClellan possession of both passes early on the 14th.
claims.rationale: Attributed command decision; Palfrey's counterfactuals are interested retrospective judgments, not estimated effects. 'Substantially unopposed' refers to Franklin's pass only.

claims.rationale: Separate gaps under different subordinates; no listed commander receives automatic sole credit. The heading rank is not adopted.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 4,500 total; the live NPS field reads 4625 total (US 2325; CS 2300;). Palfrey gives McClellan's reported 1,568 for the Turner's Gap engagement, about 530 for Franklin at Crampton's, and about 1,500 and 400 Confederate prisoners at the two gaps.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Palfrey's figures cover separate gaps and categories; they are not summed here.

open_questions: Returns, the lost order's receipt clock, casualty allocation between Turner's, Fox's and Crampton's Gaps and the effective command clocks remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family; Palfrey is one retrospective history by a former colonel of the 20th Massachusetts who says he drew on his own recollection and used advance sheets of the Official Records; his service in this campaign is not shown in the inspected text. Reports quoted inside Palfrey are not additional independently inspected families.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
